parts.text:
4
What is a reasonable estimate of the volume of one page from this examination paper?
A
60 mm3
B
600 mm3
C
6000 mm3
D
60 000 mm3

hints: Start from the size of one examination page in $\text{mm}$, roughly $200 \text{ mm}$ wide by $300 \text{ mm}$ long for A4 paper.
Remember volume is area times thickness, $V = length \times width \times thickness$, and ordinary paper is about $0.1 \text{ mm}$ thick.
Multiply your $200 \text{ mm} \times 300 \text{ mm}$ area by $0.1 \text{ mm}$ and check which power of ten it is closest to.
walkthrough: Identify what is needed: the volume of one page in $\text{mm}^3$, so estimate length, width and thickness all in $\text{mm}$.
Estimate the page area as about A4 size: $length \approx 300 \text{ mm}$ and $width \approx 200 \text{ mm}$, giving $area \approx 300 \times 200 = 60\,000 \text{ mm}^2$.
Estimate the thickness of one sheet of paper as about $0.1 \text{ mm}$, since about 100 sheets make a stack about $10 \text{ mm}$ thick.
Use $V = length \times width \times thickness \approx 300 \text{ mm} \times 200 \text{ mm} \times 0.1 \text{ mm}$.
Calculate $V \approx 60\,000 \times 0.1 = 6000 \text{ mm}^3$, which checks as a sensible small volume in $\text{mm}^3$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too small by a factor of 100 as $60 \text{ mm}^3$ would need a page area of only about $600 \text{ mm}^2$ with $0.1 \text{ mm}$ thickness.

B.explanation: Too small by a factor of 10 as $600 \text{ mm}^3$ would correspond to a tiny slip of paper, not a full examination page.

C.explanation: Matches $V \approx 200 \text{ mm} \times 300 \text{ mm} \times 0.1 \text{ mm} \approx 6000 \text{ mm}^3$ for one A4 page.

D.explanation: Too large by a factor of 10 as $60\,000 \text{ mm}^3$ would need paper about $1 \text{ mm}$ thick, like thick card.
